A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adventurer and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and technical appendices. The changed title and layout do not prevent matching the research content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification, ADE20k segmentation, COCO detection and instance-segmentation results, efficiency measurements, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds a patch-size scaling experiment in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Table 1 retain the same architecture and computation: Mamba-2 token mixing, SwiGLU channel mixing, recalculated heading-average tokens, and inter-layer flipping. The patch-size sweep varies an existing configuration without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1k classification, ADE20k semantic segmentation, and COCO 2017 detection and instance segmentation. The new patch-size experiment remains within ImageNet coverage and changes model/input configurations rather than the dataset or task.

E2.justification: The comparator identities in Tables 2–4 and the scanning and efficiency comparisons are retained. Pixel Transformer is newly discussed but is not added as an evaluated baseline. Removed COCO decoder-head labels do not establish a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Figure 5 introduces a protocol using 128×128 inputs and patch sizes 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1 for Tiny, Small, and Base models, reaching 16,384 tokens. Existing benchmark protocols and the appendix's three-stage training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Figure 5 tests how decreasing patch size affects accuracy across three model sizes, extending the evidence for very long sequences. Existing analyses of scanning directions, heading tokens, flipping, and channel mixers are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new scaling curves retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Adventurer-Base accuracy at resolution 448 from 84.0% to 84.3%, and Base/P8 from 84.6% to 84.8%, under the same listed configurations. Table 4 revises DeiT-Base values, including box AP from 47.0 to 47.2 and AP50 from 68.2 to 66.3. Figure 5 adds scaling results; most other results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The sequence and heading-average definitions are mathematically unchanged. Splitting v1's Equation 2 into v2's Equations 2 and 3 is a presentation change; neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract foregrounds efficiency against plain architectures and replaces the headline claim of 84.0% accuracy with 5.3× ViT speed with 84.3% and claimed speedups of 3.8× over Vim and 6.2× over DeiT. The central causal-modeling and architectural contributions remain.

C2.justification: New Section 4.4 interprets Adventurer's main value as enabling exploration of very long visual sequences. It develops the earlier scaling motivation through a comparison with Pixel Transformer's described resource constraints and the new pixel-sized-patch experiment. Existing mechanism explanations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes Table 2's explicit A100/DeiT benchmarking description and batch-size-128 memory setting, Table 3's input resolutions including the 640×640 Base/P8 setting, and Table 4's decoder-head distinctions. These are disclosure losses, not demonstrated experimental changes. The code link and appendix training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works, including Pixel Transformer, patchification scaling laws, iGPT, M-VAR, and ViT-linearizer, and removes Swin-UMamba. The related-work narrative remains largely intact, with additional positioning around long-sequence and pixel-level modeling.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled 'Adventurer: Optimizing Vision Mamba Architecture Designs for Efficiency.' The abstract and conclusion are revised, and a discussion subsection and acknowledgment are added. Most explanatory prose and the main section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from one-column to two-column layout. Efficiency plots move from Figure 4 to Figure 1 and become vertically stacked; the architecture diagram moves from Figure 1 to Figure 3. Figure 5 is added, Table 2 gains a token-mixer column, Tables 3–4 lose setting columns, and the appendix tables are rearranged.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 and Section 4.4 add useful evidence and interpretation for long-sequence scaling. However, v2 removes comparison settings from Tables 2–4, while its updated Table 2 accuracies coexist with unchanged 84.0% and 84.6% points in Figure 4. The revised abstract speedups also lack matching support in Table 2. These analytical gains and losses in transparency and consistency leave the net quality direction unclear.
